title: The guy opens the can/tin with one finger, meanwhile the can normally cannot be opened like that, it takes one hand to hold and the other to open

reading.marked: Frame 1 (WRONG 0:03.87): red box around the can's upper middle and the gripping fingers. Frame 2 (WRONG 0:03.90): red box around the can's top with the pull ring and the hand. Frame 3 (WRONG 0:04.17): red box around the can and the hand's upper part. Frame 4 (WRONG 0:04.47): red box around the raised index finger and the can's top with the lifted pull ring. Frame 5 (WRONG 0:05.30): red box around the can and the hand near the man's mouth. Frame 6 (RIGHT 0:05.37): green box around the can's top and the hand gripping it.
reading.right_version: Frame 6 (RIGHT 0:05.37, Video B, correct version): a woman holds a Celsius can at waist-to-chest height with one hand, the arm extended from the right side of the frame. The can is held in the hand; the second hand's action is not clearly visible.
reading.product_and_scene: The product is a silver aluminum Celsius can with a red and white 'C' logo, 'CELSIUS' lettering, and red 'PEACH VIBE' text on the front, with a pull ring on the top. In the WRONG frames (Video A) a man in a navy hoodie holds it upright at chest height in front of a brick building and trees at golden hour. The can is about as long as his hand, and his fingers wrap its lower body. In the RIGHT frame (Video B) a woman in black stands on a gravel park path and holds the can at waist-to-chest height, with the can about as long as her hand. The camera is roughly at eye level and static in each video, and it moves closer in WRONG frame 5.
reading.admin_words: Title: The guy opens the can/tin with one finger, meanwhile the can normally cannot be opened like that, it takes one hand to hold and the other to open. Frame notes: frames 1 to 5 are tagged as generated (Video A, as generated); frame 6 is tagged as correct version (Video B, a different video). Two images were sent with this generation: 'Image 1 · A17 · peach vibe front - cans usa.png' and 'Image 2 · A12 · ipiccy_image.jpg'. No other notes were given.
reading.unclear: The second hand is not visible in any WRONG frame, so I cannot tell whether it holds or opens the can. In frame 4 it is unclear whether the pull ring is lifted or just tilted by the finger. In frame 6 the second hand's position is not clearly visible. The frames are small, so fine detail of the pull ring and the finger contact is only approximate. Video B is a different person and setting, so it does not match Video A's scene directly.

frames_seen.seen: Video A, as generated. A young man in a navy hoodie stands outdoors in front of a brick building and trees, facing the camera. He holds a silver Celsius Peach Vibe can upright at chest height in the hand on the viewer's left. The pull ring on the can's top is closed. The fingers wrap the can's lower body. The other hand is not visible.

Video A, as generated. Same man, same outdoor setting, same camera distance. The can is upright at chest height and the pull ring is closed. The gripping hand is around the can's middle and lower body. The second hand is not visible.
Video A, as generated. Same man, setting and framing. The can is held upright in the same hand at chest height, with the pull ring closed on top. The second hand is not visible.

Video A, as generated. Same man and setting. The can is held upright at chest height. The index finger of the gripping hand is extended upward against the can's upper left side, near the top. The pull ring appears lifted. The second hand is not visible.

Video A, as generated. The man lifts the can toward his mouth with the hand on the viewer's left, and he looks up. The can is tilted slightly and its top is near his face. The pull ring is at the top of the can. The second hand is not visible. The camera is closer than in the earlier frames.

Video B, correct version, a different video. A woman in a black long-sleeve top stands on a gravel path in a park with bare trees and a distant figure. Her right arm reaches forward from the right side of the frame, and her hand holds a silver Celsius can at about waist-to-chest height, angled slightly.
